newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: RUGBY UNION-SPRINGBOKS TO START TITLE DEFENCE IN SCOTLAND.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SPRINGBOKS TO START TITLE DEFENCE IN SCOTLAND.

text.p: World champions South Africa will begin the defence of their title at the 1999 World Cup in Scotland.
Tuesday's draw for the first round group matches put the South Africans in pool A to be based at Murrayfield, Edinburgh.
New Zealand, finalists in 1995, will be based at Twickenham, London in pool B where they could face England who have to qualify but should take one of the two European places in the pool.
France and Wales will play their group matches at home in pool C and D respectively.
Former champions Australia, who also have to qualify, are likely to be based in Ireland in pool E.
Twenty teams, split into five groups of four, will contest the cup: Four seeds -- South Africa, New Zealand, France and Wales -- plus 16 qualifiers.
